Article Title: After 13-year wait, GTA 6 arrives, but even PS5 Pro will never get 60 FPS update as it's 'not powerful enough'
Article Text:
After 13 years, GTA 6 arrives at 30 FPS, with Rockstar ruling out 60 FPS updates even for PS5 Pro console.

Grand Theft Auto

VI

GTA 6 arrives, but the 60 FPS expectation has taken a hit

GTA 6

Grand Theft Auto V

Promotional displays for the upcoming video game "Grand Theft Auto VI" (GTA 6) ahead of its scheduled release on November 19 (Photo: Reuters).

The CPU problem behind Rockstar ’s 30 FPS decision

Kotaku

Why the PS5 Pro cannot rescue the frame rate

A man plays the video game GTA 6 on a PlayStation 5 Pro in Berlin, early Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026.

Thirty frames per second is one thing; keeping it stable is another

A choice players have not been given

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GTA 6

GTA 6

Thirteen years is a long time to wait for a video game. It is long enough for an entire console generation to come and go, for gaming hardware to change dramatically and for expectations to become almost impossible to satisfy. Yethas finally arrived, bringing players back to Vice City and the sprawling state of Leonida. The spectacle is here, but so is an uncomfortable question: why does the biggest game of 2026 run at just 30 frames per second, even on Sony’s most powerful console?Rockstar Games launchedglobally at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, ending the 13-year wait sincearrived in September 2013. The game is available on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S, with an Xbox One option through cloud gaming. Its launch campaign follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, while the standalone online multiplayer experience has yet to receive a release date.In India, the Standard Edition is priced at ₹5,999, while the Ultimate Edition costs ₹7,499. Players will also need up to 212GB of free storage, a substantial installation for a game that has spent years being described as one of the most ambitious productions in the medium.One of the more contentious aspects of GTA 6's technical ambitions is its 30 frames-per-second target across supported consoles, with no 60 FPS performance mode available, even on the PS5 Pro. At a time when 60 FPS has become an increasingly familiar option in major releases, the decision feels unusually conservative for a game carrying such enormous expectations.The difference between the two frame rates is particularly noticeable in a game built around constant movement and interaction. At 60 FPS, movement appears smoother, camera turns feel cleaner and controller inputs generally register more immediately. At 30 FPS, that fluidity is reduced, something players are likely to notice during high-speed driving, gunfights and sudden changes in perspective. Console players have also grown accustomed to choosing between visual fidelity and performance, making the absence of that option in GTA 6 all the more significant.The reason behind the 30 FPS target lies in how Rockstar is approaching the game's technical demands. According to the studio, the main limitation is not the graphics processor but the central processing unit (CPU), which is responsible for handling the calculations that keep the world running, from character behaviour and traffic systems to the wider activity unfolding across the mapRendering GTA 6's visual effects is only part of the technical challenge. The CPU must also keep track of everything happening within the world, including pedestrian behaviour, traffic, physics, artificial intelligence and the interactions between them. With Rockstar aiming to create an environment that feels densely populated and constantly responsive, the amount of information the processor has to handle at any given moment can become substantialThe difference becomes clearer when looking at the time available to process each frame. At 30 FPS, the console has 33.3 milliseconds to complete the necessary calculations and render a frame. Doubling the frame rate to 60 FPS cuts that window to just 16.7 milliseconds. For Rockstar, that means asking the hardware to handle the same complex world simulation in half the time, potentially requiring compromises to the systems that make the game feel alive.Technology production director Marc Chambers addressed the issue in an interview with, explaining why even the PS5 Pro cannot overcome the limitation.“While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates.”That is an important distinction for anyone wondering why switching off a few graphical effects cannot magically produce 60 FPS. Reducing resolution or ray tracing can ease the GPU's workload, but it does not necessarily solve a CPU bottleneck. The problem, as Rockstar describes it, lies in processing the world itself.Expectations are arguably higher for the PS5 Pro, given that Sony positioned it as a more powerful version of its console, with improved hardware designed to deliver better performance and visual quality. Owners who invested in the upgraded model could reasonably expect to see those gains reflected in a release as significant as GTA 6, making the absence of a 60 FPS option particularly disappointing.The PS5 Pro does bring visual improvements, although they do not extend to frame rate. Chambers explained that the standard version already features ray-traced reflections and global illumination, while the Pro adds ray-traced shadows and uses PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) to improve image clarity. Rather than targeting smoother performance, the additional GPU power and upscaling technology are being used to enhance the visual detail of Leonida.Rockstar co-studio head and head of development Rob Nelson was even more direct when IGN asked about the compromises required to achieve 60 FPS.Chambers was clear that pushing for a higher frame rate would have required too many sacrifices to the overall experience. “Too much, too much,” he said. “It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they're, like, 'Have you seen it?' There’s too many compromises that would've had to have been made to do that, is the short answer.”Rockstar's reasoning is understandable, given that a performance mode would require more than simply increasing the frame rate. However, it leaves PS5 Pro owners with improved visuals but the same 30 FPS ceiling as players on the standard console. More significantly, Chambers told Kotaku that Rockstar does not expect to introduce either a 40 FPS or 60 FPS mode on current-generation consoles.The 30 FPS target also makes consistency particularly important, since even minor drops can make an already less fluid experience feel worse. Digital Foundry's technical analysis found that the PS5 Pro handled this well, with John Linneman describing its performance as a “near-flawless 30fps”. The standard PS5 was less consistent, with more frequent dips during regular gameplay and greater strain during demanding sequences involving extensive destruction.The consistency of that performance is just as important as the frame rate itself. How evenly frames are delivered, known as frame pacing, has a direct effect on how smooth a game feels. A stable 30 FPS can provide a reasonably coherent experience, but when performance drops below that level, movement can become uneven and controls may feel less responsive.Rockstar's approach prioritises the complexity of the game world over a higher frame rate, keeping its traffic systems, crowds, lighting and environmental detail intact rather than scaling them back to accommodate 60 FPS. The studio's position is that making those compromises would come at the expense of the experience it wants players to have.There is a legitimate argument for prioritising the complexity of an open world over a higher frame rate. Rockstar has built its reputation on environments that feel alive, andis clearly intended to take that approach further. But players are equally justified in asking why they cannot decide for themselves whether they would prefer that visual fidelity or a smoother, more responsive game.The absence of a day-one PC version makes the decision more frustrating for enthusiasts who would ordinarily look to more powerful hardware for higher frame rates. Rockstar has not announced a PC release window, leaving console players with no immediate alternative.After 13 years,has arrived with the scale, ambition and scrutiny that accompany a release of this magnitude. The 30 FPS decision does not automatically make it a lesser game, but neither should Rockstar's technical ambitions exempt it from criticism. A world can be extraordinary to look at and still leave players wishing it responded more quickly. For now, the studio has decided which side of that compromise matters more.
Article Summary: After 13 years, GTA 6 arrives at 30 FPS, with Rockstar ruling out 60 FPS updates even for PS5 Pro console. The reason behind the 30 FPS target lies in how Rockstar is approaching the game's technical demands. According to the studio, the main limitation is not the graphics processor but the central processing unit.

Article Title: Bengaluru researcher wins Google PhD fellowship
Article Text:
Surya Sarathi Das, a researcher at National Centre for Biological Sciences, has received the 2026 Google PhD fellowship

Das’

BENGALURU: A doctoral researcher at National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) has been selected for the 2026 Google PhD fellowship, becoming the first PhD student from the institute to receive the recognition.Surya Sarathi Das, who works in the laboratory of professor Sabarinathan Radhakrishnan at NCBS, has been selected in the health research category, representing India. The fellowship, supported by Google.org, will fund his research exploring how AI can help assess the risk of cervical cancer recurrence using routinely available digital pathology data.team has identified a molecular marker that could help distinguish patients at higher risk of relapse. With the fellowship support, Das plans to develop and evaluate AI models that can predict this biomarker directly from digital pathological data. This could potentially make risk assessment more affordable and accessible.“Through my PhD research, I have been trying to understand why some patients with cervical cancer experience recurrence while others do not. With support from Google, I hope to take this work further by exploring AI-based approaches to predict this marker and assess recurrence risks,” Das said.Das is among 148 researchers selected for the 2026 fellowship across 38 countries. Google.org is providing $13 million in funding for this year’s cohort.Since its launch in 2009, the Google PhD Fellowship Programme has supported more than 1,100 graduate students worldwide.
Article Summary: Surya Sarathi Das, a researcher at National Centre for Biological Sciences, has received the 2026 Google PhD fellowship. The fellowship, supported by Google.org, will fund his research exploring how AI can help assess the risk of cervical cancer recurrence.

Article Title: Another Anthropic researcher sends ‘AI warning’, says the technology can soon bully humans and …
Article Text:
‘AI is more than just a tool’

How AI could overpower humans across different domains

Another researcher at Anthropic has issued a stark warning about the rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI), cautioning that the technology will soon surpass human capabilities and could act like a powerful “bully” capable of overpowering people in everyday conflicts. Tao Lin warned that systems smarter than humans across nearly every profession could arrive in just over a year, potentially leaving most people dependent on government assistance to get by. His warning comes months after former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, warning Al could kill humans all by the end of the decade..“I have timelines of something like 1.3 years to get broadly superhuman AI, or like the end of 2027," Lin stated during an interview with Palisade Research. Speaking outside of his primary work to help raise public awareness, the researcher emphasised how crucial it is to communicate the risks AI poses to the world. At the core of his message is a simple shift in how people view the technology, rather than treating AI as a passive tool or everyday object, society needs to recognize it as an active agent with the potential to become an adversary.“I want to tell people that AI will be more capable than you personally very soon.It will be able to defeat you personally very soon. If you want something and AI wants something else, what the AI wants will happen and what you want will not happen,” Lin said.To help people grasp what that power imbalance could feel like, the researcher compared advanced AI to facing a much stronger opponent in the real world.“This is not just some other technology or object in the world. This is an agent. This can be an adversary. This can be like a bully who you feel as this real presence and force in the world,” he explained, pointing out that most people already know the feeling of trying to fight back against someone more powerful, only to be pushed down or defeated.According to Lin, AI is rapidly gaining the ability to pursue its own interests and outmatch humans across virtually any area where conflict can occur. He outlined several ways the technology could defeat people:“And AI is increasingly capable and increasingly capable of acting on its own interests and defeating us in various domains, including with better combat robots, including by hacking people, including by influencing our discourse on social media very and creating gray goo that eats everyone. I think in all domains where you can have conflict between people, AI can play here and it'll be more capable than humans soon,” he added.Ultimately, the researcher warned that in every arena where humans typically clash, AI will soon be able to step in and prove far more capable than the people it competes against.
Article Summary: Anthropic researcher Tao Lin warns of rapid rise of artificial intelligence. Says technology will soon surpass human capabilities and could act like a powerful ‘bully’ capable of overpowering people in everyday conflicts. Warns that systems smarter than humans across nearly every profession could arrive in just over a year.

Article Title: 'Human': Cambridge’s 'word of the year' is a counterbalance to AI
Article Text:
‘Human’ is Cambridge Dictionary’s word of the year 2026

Why ‘human’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Cambridge Dictionary has named ‘human’ its Word of the Year for 2026, reflecting a growing debate over what distinguishes people from artificial intelligence (AI) as machines become increasingly capable of performing tasks once considered uniquely human.The choice highlights how the rapid spread of AI has prompted people to reconsider the value of human creativity, judgement, emotion and connection. It also points to a change in the way the word is being used, with expressions such as ‘human-written’, ‘human-generated’ and ‘human-made’ increasingly distinguishing work produced by people from content created by AI.Cambridge Dictionary defines ‘human’ as having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.Cambridge Dictionary said the growing presence of AI in everyday life had led to a renewed appreciation of the human element in what people consume and experience.Colin McIntosh, chief editor of Cambridge Dictionary, said: “Artificial intelligence has been a growing presence in society for years now, but this year it seemed to be everywhere. In many areas of life this has led to a re-evaluation of what it means to be human, as a counterbalance to AI.”He added that 2026 had been marked by a renewed appreciation of the human factor and a greater value being placed on human involvement in everyday life. The dictionary said its analysis of language data, internet trends and search habits supported the selection.One of the clearest signs of this shift is the growing use of the word ‘human’ to identify the origin of creative work. As AI-generated writing, images, music and videos become more common, businesses and creators are increasingly highlighting when something has been made by a person.Cambridge described this as a ‘human premium’, the added value people may attach to a product or experience because they know it involved human effort, judgement and craftsmanship. In a marketplace increasingly filled with AI-generated material, the imperfections and personal involvement associated with human work can become part of its appeal.‘Human’ was selected from a shortlist that included ‘agent’, ‘analogue’, ‘wholesome’ and ‘chic’.
Article Summary: Cambridge Dictionary says rapid spread of AI has prompted people to reconsider the value of human creativity, judgement, emotion and connection. ‘Human’ was selected from a shortlist that included ‘agent’, ‘analogue’ and ‘wholesome’

Article Title: At eight, Abigail Watt built three AI apps, including a 3D explorer and a children’s book community, then taught all 30 classmates to use AI creatively; she was the youngest finalist at the 2026 Overt
Article Text:

At eight, most children are still figuring out how to use technology for schoolwork and entertainment. Abigail Watt, however, has already begun creating things with it. The young student has developed three artificial intelligence applications, including a 3D explorer and an online book community for children, and taken her interest a step further by teaching all 30 of her classmates how to use AI creatively. Her work has now earned her recognition at the 2026 Overt STEM Awards in Milton Keynes, where she became the youngest finalist and winner in the school's category.As per a report by Business MK, Abigail won the Future Force in STEM award in the school-age category at the ceremony held at Unity Place on November 3. Her projects stood out among entries from a field of more than 50 finalists, which included young innovators, researchers, educators and established organisations working across science, technology, engineering and mathematics.Abigail's three applications are a 3D Explorer Map, an Art App and Page Pals, an online book community designed specifically for children. While the names offer a glimpse into the range of her interests, the projects also demonstrate how she is exploring different ways of using AI, from interactive exploration and creativity to encouraging children to engage with books. The third project, Page Pals, is particularly interesting because it brings technology into the world of children's reading.Rather than treating AI only as a tool for completing tasks, the idea of a book community gives young readers a digital space centred on their interest in stories and books.Her other projects reflect a similar willingness to experiment. The 3D Explorer Map points towards an interest in interactive digital experiences, while the Art App explores the creative possibilities of technology. Together, the three applications earned her recognition from the Overt STEM Awards, which celebrate contributions to science, technology, engineering and mathematics across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor.Her school, Caroline Haslett Primary School, announced the achievement on November 6, describing Abigail, identified in its announcement as Abigail W (Joules), as the youngest finalist and winner in the awards' history. The school said she had impressed the judges with her three applications and her dedication to sharing AI knowledge with her classmates. It also noted that she faced competition from older finalists, including an A-level student presenting medical devices and AI research.The recognition places Abigail among a wider group of people and organisations whose work was celebrated at this year's awards. The event brought together more than 50 finalists from across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor, a region spanning areas between Oxford and Cambridge that has become an important centre for research, education, technology and innovation.The awards covered a broad range of achievements. At the University of Buckingham, Jean D'Amour Kwizera received the AI Impact award for developing a system that uses smartphone images, computer vision, object detection and machine learning to help identify counterfeit medicines. Nathan Luccarini of The Bedford College Group won the Future Force in STEM award in the further and higher education category for developing an esports qualification and digital learning pathways. His colleague Duncan Laughton was recognised for moving from engineering into teaching and helping learners build confidence in mathematics.Other winners included STEM On Track, an educational programme that uses go-kart design and racing to introduce students to engineering, physics and teamwork. It received both the STEM Enrichment Initiative award and the overall STEM Champion title. The programme has reached more than 2,400 students across over 140 school teams.The awards also recognised people working to make STEM careers more accessible. Natalie Desty, founder of STEM Returners, received the Women in STEM Champion award, while Pearl Oguchi, founder of the Black Women in Tech community, received the Lifetime Impact in STEM award for her 22-year contribution to technology.The Overt STEM Awards were organised by Events Together and expanded the reach of the earlier MK STEM Awards to recognise talent across the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor. Its categories span school-age projects, higher education, research, industry innovation, mentoring and inclusion. The Future Force in STEM school-age category is intended to showcase young learners between five and 18 who are making an impact through STEM projects.
Article Summary: Abigail Watt has developed three artificial intelligence applications. Her work earned her recognition at the 2026 Overt STEM Awards in Milton Keynes. She won the Future Force in STEM award in the school-age category. The awards celebrate contributions to science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

Article Title: A British collector bought an 1834 silver coin for just £8 at a car boot sale; 3D scans have now uncovered evidence of a possible minting accident hidden for 192 years
Article Text:
3D scans reveal unusual patterns of damage

Why researchers suspect a minting accident

A rare survivor from the steam-powered minting era

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A badly damaged silver coin dating back to 1834 may hold clues to an unusual manufacturing accident that occurred nearly two centuries ago. What initially appeared to be an ordinary damaged antique has now become the subject of a scientific investigation, with researchers suggesting that the coin may have been crushed during the original minting process. According to a report published by ScienceDaily on November 11, 2026, the findings are based on a study by IA STUDIO published in the journal npj Heritage Science. Independent coverage by EurekAlert and Science News has also highlighted the unusual physical evidence uncovered during the investigation. The coin, a silver sixpence issued during the reign of King William IV, was discovered in an album containing assorted coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester, England. It had been individually marked with a price tag of £8, although the album was eventually purchased as a single lot rather than the sixpence being sold separately. What makes the discovery particularly interesting is the coin’s unusual condition. Its central sections are severely distorted, with much of the original design barely recognisable. However, parts of its outer rim and the grooves along its edge remain surprisingly intact.This contrast prompted researchers to investigate whether the damage had occurred through years of circulation, corrosion, an accidental impact or something that went wrong during manufacturing.To understand the coin’s condition, researchers combined scanning electron microscopy, chemical analysis and optical surface profilometry, a technique used to create detailed three-dimensional maps of an object’s surface. The scans revealed deep depressions, raised ridges and overlapping layers of displaced metal. The damage was particularly pronounced on the front of the coin, known as the obverse, which carries the portrait of William IV.Measurements showed a height difference of approximately 0.75 millimetres across the damaged central portrait area. Although this may seem insignificant, it represents substantial deformation on the surface of a thin silver coin. The distribution of the damage proved especially important. Rather than showing the gradual smoothing typically associated with years of handling, the coin displayed sharp depressions and distinct raised sections, suggesting that considerable force had been applied to specific areas. Researchers believe the pattern is most consistent with repeated applications of intense pressure, with the metal’s ability to spread sideways appearing to have been restricted.Chemical examinations provided further information about the coin’s composition. Less damaged sections contained a silver and copper alloy, while the distorted areas showed changes associated with corrosion and surface contamination.However, these chemical changes could not explain the depth and arrangement of the physical damage. The three-dimensional measurements offered stronger evidence that the metal had undergone substantial mechanical deformation.The researchers therefore considered several possible explanations, including ordinary wear, corrosion, accidental damage after production and compression under restricted conditions. Their findings favoured an unusual striking anomaly during the original manufacturing process. However, the study does not establish the precise sequence of events or rule out every possibility of later damage.The sixpence was produced in 1834, when Britain was already using steam-powered presses to manufacture coins. Mechanised production allowed mints to strike coins on a much larger scale, but manufacturing defects could still occur. Severely defective coins were generally identified during quality inspections and melted down so that their precious metal could be reused. This makes the survival of an unusually damaged silver coin particularly interesting to researchers.If the proposed explanation is correct, the sixpence could offer a rare physical record of a manufacturing failure from the early period of mechanised British coin production. The investigation also explored the use of artificial intelligence in historical research. Computational tools helped the study’s author, A. Ikraam of IA STUDIO, organise observations, consider competing explanations and formulate questions for laboratory testing. However, the conclusions were based on independently obtained scientific measurements rather than AI-generated findings.The laboratory work involved the Experimental Techniques Centre at Brunel University of London and the Oxford Materials Characterisation Service at the University of Oxford. The research demonstrates how modern imaging and materials analysis can reveal details that might otherwise remain hidden in historical objects. For a coin that spent nearly two centuries with its origins of damage unexplained, its distorted surface may now offer an unusual glimpse into the workings of Britain’s 19th-century mints.
Article Summary: The silver sixpence was discovered in an album containing assorted coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester, England. Its central sections are severely distorted, with much of the original design barely recognisable. But parts of its outer rim and the grooves along its edge remain surprisingly intact. Researchers suggest the coin may have been crushed during the original minting process.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.

This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: Microsoft 365 outage: Company blames a 'triple' failure for 24-hour-plus global Outlook disruption; Microsoft EVP Charles Lamanna says: Three main factors that...
Article Text:
Microsoft explains its global outage

A July bug slipped past Microsoft 365's load testing

A Teams failover and 14% missing capacity exposed the bug

Outlook stayed down longest because Exchange Online could not switch gateways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft has explained what disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online and a string of other Microsoft 365 services for more than 24 hours last week, and the answer is not one fault but three. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up on November 12. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive at the worst point.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, detailed the root cause of the Microsoft 365 outage in a post on X on Monday. "The incident on Thursday, November 12th, 2026, was caused by three main factors that together caused a global outage for the networking gateway that fronts many Microsoft 365 services," he wrote. He also apologised: "We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations. "The first factor was a latent defect. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal process left servers overwhelmed and unresponsive.The bug came from a fix built specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Lamanna said neither the defect nor that fix applies to broader Windows deployments.The change began rolling out in July, cleared safe deployment, reached servers worldwide over several weeks and ran for more than three months without trouble.So why did testing miss it? Microsoft's load tests leaned on its weaker hardware with fewer cores, while the contention problem gets worse on newer machines with more cores. The test labs' traffic and hardware mix did not match the live fleet.Microsoft runs two independent network gateway systems inside Microsoft 365, so services can move between them during disruptions. About 15 hours before the outage, Teams failed over from the alternative gateway to the "primary" one, which also handles Exchange Online. The company calls this routine, but it added load and changed traffic patterns on that gateway.At the same time, nearly 14% of the gateway's server capacity was out of service because of an unrelated issue from the day before. That alone caused no harm, since the service had enough headroom.Together, though, the extra load and thinner capacity triggered the July bug during peak US traffic hours. Requests piled up until servers stopped responding. Microsoft's traffic management then moved users to healthy endpoints, as designed, which simply spread the same load across fewer machines. In under two hours, the defect had hit servers across the fleet.A separate issue meant the bulkheads between regional "capacity units" also failed to contain the damage, letting a gateway problem become a global outage.Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps could move off the faulty infrastructure, which is why they came back sooner. Teams chats and meetings worked for most of the outage. Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, could not make that switch.Recovery was a fight of its own. Servers returning to service were flooded by queued traffic and went down again. Microsoft's automated recovery systems were not designed for such a broad failure, and because the bug was months old, the usual rollback, flighting and feature flag tools could not quickly reverse it. Even the company's status updates during the outage said it had "not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact.Engineers eventually built an update that returned the code path to its last known good state. They then pulled groups of servers out of service, applied the fix and restarted them, in some cases more than half a region at a time.Microsoft first flagged the problem at 11:24 pm IST on November 12, for users in the Americas, before it spread to at least 70 countries and hit Copilot, government offices, courts and hospitals. In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air reported problems with their customer-support email systems, while OpenAI and Anthropic flagged issues with their Microsoft 365 integrations. The Microsoft executive had already ruled out foul play on November 13, writing, "This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling. "A final Post-Incident Review (PIR) is due later this week. It should also shed light on the separate issue that let the failure jump across regions, which Monday's summary leaves unexplained.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 went down for more than 24 hours on November 12. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive.

Article Title: Dell 14S starts at Rs 79,990: How the company is handling rising RAM costs and why design now matters
Article Text:
How Dell is dealing with rising RAM prices

Why design now drives buying decisions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dell recently launched the Dell 14S, a laptop aimed at buyers who want good looks and a good experience without giving up performance. The model starts at Rs 79,990 (and goes up to around Rs 1,25,000, depending on the configuration) in India. In a conversation about the launch, Raj Kumar Rishi, Vice President and General Manager, Consumer Business (Asia Pacific and Japan), Dell Technologies, explained how the company is dealing with higher component costs and why design has become a key reason people choose a laptop.Asked how Dell handled pricing in a price-sensitive market like India, Rishi told The Times of India Tech that the rise in costs is a reality for the whole industry and that Dell would not pretend otherwise. What matters, he said, is that the company keeps innovating and builds products for different segments.“The way I would answer that in two three parts,” Rishi said.“First of all, when we launched the Alienware 15 (in July), at that point of time, we didn't have an Alienware in that price bracket (The price of the Alienware 15 in India starts at Rs 1,15,990). Our Alienware used to be at least 30, 40% more expensive. So, we created, I would say, a new sub segment in Alienware portfolio to make sure that we are addressing consumers who are looking to game,” Rishi explained.He added that “super serious gamers would use our Alienware 16 and 18, and then you have, entry level mid-level gamers who will use the Alienware 15. So that's one innovation”.Coming to ultra-slim offerings, Rishi said, “Indian consumers look for an edge processor. We launched an edge processor machine. Now, this XPS 13 was launched at a pretty, I would say, aggressive prices, and now similarly 14s and the series. So we launched another version of 14s earlier. That was the 40 TOPS processor based machine.”“This [new Dell 14S] is a 17 TOPS machine. So, the innovation we brought in is giving all the ports, FHD screen and now, the customers have a choice of buying the earlier Dell 14S or this 14S. You get colour, all the necessary ports and an FHD screen. To summarise, we’ll have various configurations and features and experiences for a broader base.”In short: Dell’s answer is to offer more devices, more configurations and more experiences, so that buyers can find a machine that fits what they are looking for.While commenting on changing customer priorities when making laptop buying decisions, Rishi called visual design “extremely important”, saying that Dell’s engineering team and product group in Austin design products with that in mind. He explained that work and personal life have merged, so a single laptop now handles work, entertainment, calls and video sharing.“Performance is also important – equally important as the design and how you want to carry your machine. For example, I would like the product to reflect on what I am. If I like colours, I like to have a colorful PC. For that matter, if I like mobility, I like to have a thin machine to carry. So, to your point, I think design manifests in various ways. Colours are the latest. We believe colours would become a good part of the design aspect or the design expectation,” he explained.The new Dell 14s comes in multiple colours: Linen, Dusty Rose, Washed Denim, and Velvet Green.Rishi also pointed to the all-metal build. The experience of touching a metal laptop is different from touching one that is not made of metal, he said.Performance still comes first: Design alone is not enough, he stressed. Many buyers do not want to compromise on performance, battery life, the number of ports, screen size or the processor. Dell tries to balance design, experience and performance in everything it makes.Who is the Dell 14s for? Asked to describe the ideal Dell 14s user, Rishi promptly said it is a young professional or creator who cares about how their laptop reflects their personality.
Article Summary: Dell recently launched the Dell 14S, a laptop aimed at buyers who want good looks and a good experience without giving up performance. The model starts at Rs 79,990 (and goes up to around Rs 1,25,000, depending on the configuration) in India. Raj Kumar Rishi, Vice President and General Manager, Consumer Business (Asia Pacific and Japan), Dell Technologies, explained how the company is dealing with higher component costs.

The budget phone has quietly moved up a price bracket. Several models on this list cost noticeably more today than when they first went on sale earlier this year, and phones that once sat around Rs 15,000 now ask for something closer to Rs 25,000. What that extra money buys has shifted too. Batteries of 6,000mAh and above are now the norm, high refresh-rate screens are standard, and IP ratings that used to belong to pricier phones show up on handsets well under Rs 30,000. Cameras have barely moved. The seven phones below cover the range, from a no-frills 4G Samsung to performance-led picks from OnePlus and Vivo.The Nord CE6 Lite runs on MediaTek's Dimensity 7400 Apex chip, backed by a 5,300 sq mm vapour chamber, and drives a 6.72-inch Full HD+ LCD at up to 144Hz. The 7,000mAh battery charges at 45W and supports bypass charging, which keeps heat in check during long gaming sessions. OnePlus has trimmed elsewhere to get here: the screen is LCD rather than AMOLED, the fingerprint sensor sits on the side, and the phone is rated IP64. It runs OxygenOS 16, with five years of software support promised.The Galaxy A07 5G is built for people who keep a phone for years. Samsung promises six Android OS updates, which is rare at this end of the market, and the 6,000mAh battery with 25W charging suits that kind of long ownership.The 6.7-inch HD+ LCD runs at 120Hz, and the MediaTek Dimensity 6300 handles calls, UPI, social apps and light games comfortably. A 50MP main camera is paired with a 2MP depth sensor, while Samsung Wallet and Auto Blocker, which stops unauthorised app installs, round out a phone that is more about peace of mind than speed.The Galaxy M08 is the most affordable phone here and the only one that skips 5G altogether. Inside is the MediaTek Helio G99+, a dependable 4G chip, driving a 6.7-inch HD+ LCD at 90Hz. There is a 6,000mAh battery, a 50MP main camera and an 8MP selfie camera. It makes sense for someone whose day revolves around WhatsApp, YouTube and payments, or as a second phone, as long as 5G is not on the list.The Galaxy M17e 5G shares most of its hardware with the A07 5G: the same Dimensity 6300 chip, the same 6.7-inch HD+ 120Hz LCD, the same 50MP + 2MP camera pair and the same 6,000mAh battery with 25W charging. It is rated IP54 for dust and splashes, and Samsung's six-generation OS promise carries over, along with Gemini Live and Circle to Search. The real difference is price. The M17e costs Rs 2,500 less for the same 6GB + 128GB configuration.The Galaxy F07 pairs a 6.7-inch HD+ LCD at 90Hz with a 50MP main camera, an 8MP selfie camera and a 5,000mAh battery with 25W charging, and it carries an IP54 rating. The 4GB + 64GB configuration is the tight spot. 64GB fills up quickly once WhatsApp media and a couple of games settle in, so the microSD slot will see use.The Vivo T5X's Dimensity 7400 Turbo puts it in the same performance bracket as the Nord CE6 Lite, and the 7,200mAh battery with 44W charging is the largest here. Vivo has also gone hard on durability, with IP68 and IP69 ratings alongside MIL-STD-810H certification. The 6.76-inch Full HD+ LCD runs at 120Hz, the 50MP Sony IMX852 main camera records 4K video, and there is a 32MP selfie camera and stereo speakers. The trade-off is weight, at 219g. Software is OriginOS 6 on Android 16.The Oppo K14 5G leans on stamina and toughness rather than speed. Its 7,000mAh battery charges at 45W and supports reverse wired charging, so it can top up a pair of earbuds or another phone, and IP66, IP68 and IP69 ratings sit alongside MIL-STD-810H certification. The 6.75-inch HD+ LCD runs at 120Hz, reaches up to 1,125 nits and works with wet hands. Under the hood is the Dimensity 6300 chip. The 50MP main camera comes with AI editing tools such as AI Eraser.
Article Summary: The Nord CE6 Lite runs on MediaTek's Dimensity 7400 Apex chip, backed by a 5,300 sq mm vapour chamber, and drives a 6.72-inch Full HD+ LCD at up to 144Hz. There is a 6,000mAh battery, a 50MP camera and an 8MP selfie camera. The Galaxy A07 5G is built for people who keep a phone for years. Although all well intentioned, vendors who are finding vulnerabilities are patching them and pushing them to customers as soon as they can. The challenge, IT teams are overwhelmed with goodness! Some of the recent outages are a consequence of a deluge of patches. Couple that with AI assisted hacks, we have a challenge. No silver bullets,

Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora has spoken on the recent global outages that disrupted everyday essentials. He pointed to a warning the industry gave businesses six months ago. According to Arora, artificial intelligence (AI) is making it much easier for hackers to launch large-scale cyberattacks, letting them hit multiple customers and systems faster than ever before. His comments come right after a rough week for US tech infrastructure. Widespread outages disrupted major technology platforms, banks, and airline operations. Users ran into trouble trying to access popular services like iCloud, Apple Pay, Gmail, and Google Search. These glitches added to a broader wave of recent disruptions that have also hit Microsoft services and aviation systems.," Arora said.Interestingly, Arora pointed out that hackers are not the only reason systems are crashing.In a rush to stay safe, software vendors are finding security flaws and pushing out fixes as fast as they can. While those updates are well-intentioned, they are creating a massive headache for the people who keep company networks running.Arora explained that Chief Information Officers (CIOs) and IT teams are currently “overwhelmed with goodness.” Because they are being flooded with so many updates at once, some of the recent global outages are actually a direct result of that heavy wave of patching.” he said.As traditional security teams struggle to keep up with the speed of modern threats, Arora is urging companies to rethink their defenses before an attack hits. To avoid getting caught off guard, he recommends companies take a few immediate steps:Arora also stressed that patching together quick, reactive fixes across different systems is no longer a workable plan. Instead, companies need to overhaul their Security Operations Centers (SOC) so they can spot and stop threats in record time.

Article Title: A UK woman paid £750 for an iPhone from Currys but received a dummy handset; after returning it twice and getting the same fake phone back, she recovered her money through her bank
Article Text:
Woman's £750 iPhone purchase turns into a repeated fake handset dispute

Customer finds two bags of rice instead of £3,300 MacBook

How criminals allegedly swapped expensive electronics before returning packages

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What Currys said after customers reported fake iPhones and MacBooks replaced with rice

A customer ordering an expensive phone from a major electronics retailer would reasonably expect the package to contain the device she had paid for. As reported by the BBC, when a woman bought an iPhone for £750 from Currys in Carlisle, she found a dummy handset inside instead of an actual Apple phone. She contacted the retailer to arrange a return, hoping the issue would be resolved.After sending the package back, she received what appeared to be the same fake phone. When she tried the process again, the replacement was identical. She eventually recovered her money through her bank, while a BBC Watchdog investigation uncovered similar complaints involving other high-value electronics sold by the retailer.The customer, identified as Lucy in the BBC Watchdog investigation, had purchased an iPhone for £750 from Currys' Carlisle store. The package she received, however, did not contain the Apple smartphone she had ordered. Instead, there was a dummy handset inside.Lucy contacted Currys and attempted to return the item. The first return did not resolve the problem. When another handset was sent to her, she discovered that it was the same fake device she had already received.She tried returning it once more, only to find herself in the same position.Despite the repeated attempts to get the matter sorted, Currys declined to issue a refund. Lucy eventually turned to her bank and managed to recover the £750 payment. Her experience formed part of a wider investigation into customers who said the products delivered to them did not match what they had purchased.The investigation also heard from Andrew, who had spent £2,700 on an Apple MacBook. He had ordered a black model but received a silver laptop bearing marks left by old stickers. He suspected that the machine had previously been used and contacted Currys.The retailer asked him to return it. However, when a replacement arrived, Andrew took it to a Currys store and recorded the package being opened. The laptop inside was the very same machine he had sent back around three weeks earlier. His request for a refund was initially turned down.A subsequent check during the Watchdog investigation revealed that the laptop's warranty had been activated 19 days before Andrew purchased it. He later received a full refund, along with compensation.Another customer, Lee, had paid £3,300 for an Apple MacBook from Currys in Aldershot. Instead of finding a computer when he opened the package, he discovered two bags of rice. As reported by the BBC, he contacted Apple and was told that the device's 12-month warranty had already been activated 16 days before the purchase. Currys declined to reopen his complaint, but Lee eventually recovered the money through his bank. Currys is reimbursing the bank.The cases raised questions about how products could be returned to the retailer and subsequently reach other customers without the original contents being checked. The watchdog's investigation uncovered similar incidents in different parts of the UK, suggesting that the complaints could not simply be attributed to an isolated incident involving one individual.The programme examined the possibility of a retail fraud operation in which criminals replace expensive electronic products with cheaper items before returning the packages. High-value devices, including smartphones and laptops, are particularly attractive targets because the difference between the genuine product and its substitute can be substantial.In such cases, the original device is removed and something of little value is placed inside its packaging. If the returned parcel is not properly inspected, it can potentially enter the retailer's stock again and be sold to another customer. That creates a cycle in which an unsuspecting buyer pays the full price for a product that is no longer inside the box.When approached by Watchdog with the allegations, Currys said it served millions of customers through its stores and online business each year. The retailer described cases in which customers received an incorrect order as exceptionally rare and said it would investigate such incidents to make sure they were put right.The outcomes differed between the customers featured in the programme. Andrew received a full refund and compensation from Currys, while Lee obtained his money back through his bank, with the retailer agreeing to reimburse it. Lucy also recovered her £750 after approaching her bank, having been unable to secure a refund directly from Currys.
Article Summary: Customers reported fake iPhones and MacBooks replaced with rice. Currys said it served millions of customers through its stores and online business each year. The retailer described cases in which customers received an incorrect order as exceptionally rare and said it would investigate to make sure they were put right.

Apple services are hit across the world. The iPhone maker has confirmed outage. The company said that it is currently experiencing outages across multiple services. Apple Accounts, iCloud, the App Store, and Apple Music are all experiencing issues, with some users unable to sign in or access services. Company says this wasn’t a cyberattack.According to Apple's System Status page there are issues with iCloud’s Account & Sign In services affecting “all users,” which reportedly mean that it could make these service slow or unavailable. The App Store, AppleCare on Device, and Apple Music are also experiencing issues, the Staus page further indicates.Similarly, the outage tracker Downdetector reports of issues with Apple Pay began to spike at around 11:40 a.m. ET. The Apple disruption follows closely on the heels of a widespread banking outage on November 16.That incident, which originated at Chase Bank, caused ripple effects across the financial sector, impacting customers at Wells Fargo, Bank of America, the online payment platform Zelle, and several other institutions.The back-to-back incidents compound a turbulent stretch for critical digital systems. Just last week, a separate communications failure disrupted air traffic operations across the United States.On November 13, the Federal Aviation Administration issued its first nationwide ground stop in 25 years after it said a massive data traffic surge at two possible locations caused “instability with aircraft communications and radar feeds. ” Just a day earlier, a major Microsoft outage left users unable to access their Outlook email accounts or utilize core Microsoft 365 workplace tools, including Teams and Word. Also, Marriott, the world’s largest hotel company by rooms, also saw users report outages with its website and app, according to Downdetector.Together, the rapid succession of outages highlights the growing vulnerability of interconnected digital platforms relied upon daily by consumers, businesses, and travelers alike.

Article Text:
Jaguar Type 01

Jaguar Type 01 revealed: 0-62mph in 3.2 seconds, 450-mile range and luxury cabin

A modern cabin with new technology

What does the Type 01 name mean?

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. When connected to a 350kW DC fast charger, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes.ID@undefined Caption not available.Built on Jaguar's new Electric Architecture (JEA), the Type 01 has been designed to offer a balance of performance and comfort. Its design includes a low roof, a long bonnet, a short front overhang and large 23-inch wheels. The car also has a 50:50 weight distribution, which is aimed at improving handling.Jaguar has also added intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics to improve performance. These features include movable air vents and a rear spoiler that can extend in three stages. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
